analytic_certificates.proof: Before64 no process completes: raw delivery>=4 and all first T/F durations>=60. Single T and F permit at most two starts, totaling<=10 mandatory attendance. This leaves>=54 non-attendance minutes in that prefix. After flange weld completes, its chain requires B-to-A, A-to-B, B-to-A walks, all after64 and disjoint from mandatory attendance. Last mandatory processing is full pumpQA, followed by shipping.

Before a productive hallB visit, at most three accepted components occupy/reserve ASM input and one occupies QA output. Inbound moves reserve destination capacity. QA fully attends the sole worker in A, so no additional acceptance occurs during that B visit. Two assembly starts require six distinct accepted components, exceeding four; hence at most one assembly starts per B visit. The first productive B visit must weld before any flange can return A for wash/QA, so it cannot assemble a pump. Thus n+1 B visits, each returning A before final QA. Under automatic prefix assumptions, only the first outward walk may overlap the initial prefix.

Let P=[0,64) minus required attendance, measure>=54. Reserved ASM capacity3 plus one QA output allow atmost4 accepted unconsumed components; no QA can complete while sole worker is inB. Each productive B excursion starts atmostone assembly, and the first must weld before any assembly, giving n+1 excursions and2(n+1) selected2-minute walks. Only the first selected outward walk can overlap P, by o<=2. If it does, arrival b<=66, while first required B work starts>=72, so G=[max(64,b),72) has measure>=o and is disjoint from P, selected walks and required attendance. Therefore union(P,selectedwalks,G) has measure>=54+4(n+1). Add350n disjoint required attendance and8 final shipping after the last full pumpQA. Extra unproductive early walks do not invalidate the union argument; no claim that all nonwalking idle alone is>=54 is needed.
